title: Repentance unto Life: Guidelines for Application
speaker: Mr. Nick Newton

outline.title: Review of Repentance as a Gift of Grace
subpoints: Repentance is a gift of the gospel, not a work for salvation.
Distinction between sorrow of the world and godly sorrow.
Faith alone justifies, but faith is never alone.
The necessity of repentance for all sinners within the new covenant.

outline.title: Perceiving the Danger and Filthiness of Sin
subpoints: Sight and sense of sin are formed by Scripture, not just physical observation.
Unrepentant sin leads to mortal danger and divine judgment.
Examples of judgment: Sodom, Korah, Ananias and Sapphira.
The conscience as a built-in sense of God's law that can be seared.

outline.title: The Nature of Sin as Cosmic Treason
subpoints: Sin is contrary to the holy nature and righteous law of God.
Sin is odious and hated by God, violating His holiness and glory.
Rebellion against the Sovereign King is an act of treason.
Believers must mimic God's contempt for sin to achieve true repentance.

outline.title: Turning to God in Mercy
subpoints: Apprehension of God's mercy in Christ motivates grief for sin.
True repentance involves hating sin and turning from it entirely.
The goal is to walk with God in all the ways of His commandments.
Repentance is a continuous endeavor to align actions with God's holiness.

summary: This session continues the study of Chapter 15 of the Westminster Confession of Faith, focusing on the doctrine of repentance unto life. After reviewing the previous lesson's definition of repentance as a gift of grace, the teaching shifts to the practical application of this doctrine. The speaker emphasizes that repentance is not merely an emotional response but a comprehensive turning from sin to God, driven by a proper understanding of God's holiness and the severity of sin.

As we conclude this study of repentance unto life, we'll circle back one last time to 1 John 1, specifically verse 9. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just. Forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness. This last point I want to make here, verse 9 hinges on the if. No one is going to repent for us for our own sins. If we would desire the degree of salvation, repentance is a prerequisite course of equal weight as faith. Christ won't repent for us and say, oh, Nick is just a carnal Christian. Don't worry about him. I'll cover for him. There's absolutely no place for that in Christian thinking. If there isn't any genuine repentance, the genuineness of the faith is called into question. No, if we confess our sins, if we confront our wrongdoings before our Father and turn again to seek his glory, we are justified, and more importantly, he is glorified. if you find only one takeaway from these two lessons, I hope it is this. If we confess our sins, we are on the hook for the effort required of one who turns again to God. But we are much more on the hook for the unfathomable blessing of new life here and the life to come. For that, our only reaction ought to be, praise to such a glorious and merciful God. Let's close with a word of prayer. early release again. You guys got lucky two weeks in a row. Heavenly Father, thank you for revealing your truth to us in your word and blessing us with learned men to interpret it. I pray that your infinite holiness and your arc of redemptive history and the good news of your son would spur us all towards repentance unto life. I pray that these words would be edifying to all that heard them and they may be pointed only to you and your righteousness. In your son's name, amen.
